evidence: Where Meridian Persons are entitled to participate in any equity-based remuneration scheme, they must not enter into any transaction for any 'Associated Product'. An Associated Product is any product which has the effect of limiting the economic risk of participating in any entitlement a Meridian Person is eligible for under the remuneration scheme.

detail: Rule Three is drafted around 'participating in any entitlement a Meridian Person is eligible for under the remuneration scheme' rather than around vesting, so shares that have vested but remain held under the scheme or subject to a restriction are still an entitlement under it and cannot be hedged. The Policy nowhere uses the language of vesting or holding locks.
evidence: any product which has the effect of limiting the economic risk of participating in any entitlement a Meridian Person is eligible for under the remuneration scheme

detail: Once scheme shares have vested and been delivered free of restriction they arguably cease to be an 'entitlement a Meridian Person is eligible for under the remuneration scheme', taking them outside Rule Three; the same is true of shares bought on market. A collar over such shares is still a trade in Meridian Securities requiring prior written General Counsel approval, outside a Blackout Period. The boundary is untested on the face of the Policy.
evidence: Before trading in Meridian Securities outside of a Blackout Period ... Meridian Restricted Persons must, using the form at the back of this policy: seek approval from the General Counsel

detail: For a Meridian Person who is not a Restricted Person, hedging shares that are no longer an entitlement under a remuneration scheme is not prohibited and requires no approval, subject only to the insider trading ban.
evidence: Where Meridian Persons are entitled to participate in any equity-based remuneration scheme, they must not enter into any transaction for any 'Associated Product'.

section: Rule One ('Trade'); Additional Rules Three and Five
detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar is an agreement to dispose of Meridian Securities and so a trade needing General Counsel approval; if it is monetised by a loan secured on Meridian Securities it is separately caught by the Additional Rule Five ban, and if it monetises a scheme entitlement it is an Associated Product.
evidence: 'Trade' includes applying for, acquiring or disposing of securities or other financial products, or agreeing to do so.

detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy, and there is no speculative trading ban. A short sale would still be a disposal of Meridian Securities and so a trade requiring General Counsel approval for a Restricted Person.
Securities lending is not named and is not within the definition of 'Trade', which reaches only applying for, acquiring or disposing of securities or agreeing to do so.

section: What this policy applies to; Additional Rule Three
detail: CFDs are not named. A CFD over Meridian shares is a derivative in respect of securities of Meridian and so a Meridian Security, making it a trade requiring prior General Counsel approval; there is no speculative trading ban to bar it outright, but a CFD position opened and closed within three months would breach Rule Two.
evidence: options or derivatives (including futures contracts listed on a futures exchange) in respect of any securities of Meridian or its subsidiaries

detail: Outright ban with no approval route, expressly retrospective ('or continue with'), covering both loans to fund acquisition of Meridian Securities and loans in relation to which Meridian Securities may be used as security. Extended to holdings in the name of spouses, partners, dependent children, trusts where the person is trustee, and controlled companies.
evidence: Meridian Restricted Persons may not enter into or continue with any margin loan arrangements to fund the acquisition of Meridian Securities or in relation to which Meridian Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan.

detail: Additional Rule Five binds only Meridian Restricted Persons; the Policy is silent on margin loans by other Meridian Persons.

Granting security over Meridian Securities is not itself a 'Trade', but the second limb of Additional Rule Five bans any arrangement 'in relation to which Meridian Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan'. The noun in the sentence is 'margin loan arrangements', so a purist could argue a bespoke bank facility is outside it, but the second limb and the stated rationale (forced sale in a Blackout Period) point the other way.
evidence: any margin loan arrangements to fund the acquisition of Meridian Securities or in relation to which Meridian Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan

detail: No encumbrance or pledge rule applies to Meridian Persons outside the Restricted Person population, and granting security is not a 'Trade'.

The loan leg of a funded collar is a loan in relation to which Meridian Securities are used as security against repayment, which Additional Rule Five prohibits for every Restricted Person, including through a spouse, dependent child, trust or controlled company, with no approval, hardship or exceptional-circumstances route. The General Counsel's exceptional-circumstances discretion is expressed only in relation to Blackout Period trading, not Rule Five.
evidence: This is because the terms of such a loan may require the sale of Meridian Securities during a Blackout Period or while the Meridian Restricted Person is in possession of inside information.

detail: Secured financing is regulated only through Additional Rule Five, which applies to Meridian Restricted Persons alone.

Acquiring and then selling Meridian Securities within three months is banned for everyone, subject only to advance General Counsel approval in exceptional circumstances. There is no carve-out for shares acquired on vesting under an incentive plan.
evidence: Meridian Persons must not engage in short term trading (i.e. acquiring and then selling Meridian Securities within a three month period), unless there are exceptional circumstances discussed and approved in advance by Meridian's General Counsel.

detail: There is no separate derivatives rule, but 'dealing' is defined to capture the full range of transactions, arrangements and financial products available in connection with the Company's securities, with an express substance over form approach and no venue limit. An OTC put and call is therefore a dealing needing prior written approval under section 5.4, and a hedging approval under 5.8, and is barred in blackout periods.
evidence: When the expression 'deal' or 'dealing' is used in this Policy, it is intended to capture the full range of transactions, arrangements and financial products that are available in connection with a company's securities. ... The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.

detail: Employees who are not Restricted Persons or Connected Persons are subject only to the insider trading prohibition, any Company notice not to deal, and the Front Page Test; sections 5.1 to 5.8 do not apply to them.
evidence: Certain aspects of this Policy apply only to Restricted Persons and their Connected Persons.

detail: Hedging Company securities is permitted with prior written approval, sought from the Group General Counsel & Company Secretary and determined by the relevant Approving Officer under section 5.5. There is no outright ban and no security-state limitation in the operative words.
evidence: Restricted Persons and Connected Persons must not, without prior written approval, hedge Company securities.

detail: Unusually, the Policy does not absolutely prohibit hedging unvested plan securities; it gives that as the illustration of what counts as hedging and subjects it to the same prior written approval. Approval would still have to survive the Front Page Test and the terms of the relevant equity plan, which are outside the Policy.
evidence: for example, entering into arrangements that have the effect of limiting the economic risk in connection with unvested securities issued pursuant to a staff or director equity plan

detail: Section 5.8 binds only Restricted Persons and Connected Persons; hedging by other Employees is not addressed.

Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or collar-plus-loan limits the economic risk associated with holding Company securities and so needs hedging approval, and if secured it also needs approval under 5.7. The tension is section 5.2, which names forward contracts as an example of prohibited short-term dealing, so a monetisation structure must be long-dated to avoid that ban.
evidence: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 12 month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

detail: Outright ban with no approval route, defined by reference to borrowing a security and selling it to buy back lower. The exceptional-circumstances relief in 5.3 covers only blackout and short-term dealing, not short selling.
evidence: Short sell the Company's securities. Short selling refers to the practice of borrowing a security and selling it in the hope that it can be bought back at a lower price at some time in the future to close out the short position.

detail: The short-selling ban in section 5.2 is addressed only to Restricted Persons and Connected Persons.

Securities lending arrangements are named in the chapeau to 5.7 and any dealing in connection with one requires prior written approval, treated under the section 5.5 process. Lending stock to facilitate a short position would still run into the 5.2 short-selling ban.
evidence: Restricted Persons and Connected Persons must obtain prior written approval for any proposed dealing in the Company's securities in connection with a margin lending or securities lending arrangement

detail: CFDs are not named. A CFD is a financial product available in connection with the Company's securities and so a dealing requiring approval, but a short CFD would breach the short-selling ban and a CFD closed within 12 months would breach the short-term dealing ban, so approval is unlikely.
evidence: it is intended to capture the full range of transactions, arrangements and financial products that are available in connection with a company's securities

detail: Margin lending is not banned. Entering into a margin lending arrangement, transferring securities into an existing margin loan account, and selling securities to satisfy a margin call each require prior written approval under the section 5.5 process.
evidence: entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities; transferring securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account; selling securities in the Company to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan

detail: Section 5.7 binds only Restricted Persons and Connected Persons.

The grant of a mortgage, charge, lien or other encumbrance or third party interest over Company securities is expressly listed as requiring prior written approval, not prohibited. The bullet is general in terms even though the chapeau frames 5.7 around margin lending and securities lending arrangements.
evidence: the grant of a mortgage, charge, lien or other encumbrance or third party interest over the Company's securities.

detail: No encumbrance rule applies to Employees who are not Restricted Persons or Connected Persons.

Secured financing over Company securities is permitted with prior written approval: the encumbrance bullet in 5.7(a) covers any mortgage, charge, lien, encumbrance or third party interest, and the Policy then carves the lender's enforcement sale out of the blackout, short-term and approval rules. Section 6 does not disapply 5.7 or 5.8, so approval for the arrangement itself is always needed.
evidence: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

detail: Secured financing is regulated only through section 5.7, which binds Restricted Persons and Connected Persons.

A twelve-month rule, far longer than the market-standard three months, and it reaches beyond on-market round trips to 'other short-term dealings', with forward contracts given as the example. Relief is available only on an exceptional-circumstances application under 5.3 (severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order). Participation in an equity plan is excluded from 5.2, but dealing in plan securities once they cease to be held under the plan is not.
evidence: Deal in the Company's securities on a short-term trading basis. Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 12 month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

detail: The short-term dealing ban applies only to Restricted Persons and Connected Persons.

section: Introduction and purpose; Trading outside black-out periods
detail: Restricted Securities expressly include listed derivatives in respect of Auckland Airport securities, including listed futures. Buying or selling one, or agreeing to do so, is a trade requiring written consent from the General Manager Corporate Affairs and is barred in blackout periods.
evidence: any other listed securities of Auckland Airport or its subsidiaries, and any listed derivatives (including futures contracts listed on an authorised futures exchange) in respect of Auckland Airport securities, from time to time.

detail: The Policy reaches only listed instruments. 'Trade' means buying or selling listed securities or agreeing to do so, and the definition of Restricted Securities extends to listed derivatives only. An OTC put and call written by a bank is therefore outside the definition of Restricted Securities and outside the consent and blackout regime, unless it is an associated product over unvested plan entitlements or, in substance, an agreement to sell listed shares.
evidence: In this policy 'trade' includes buying or selling listed securities, or agreeing to do so, whether as principal or agent, but it does not include subscription for, or the issue of, new securities.

detail: Employees and officers who are not Restricted Persons need no consent and are not subject to blackout periods; only the insider trading prohibition, the associated products rule and the one-month short term rule apply.
evidence: In addition to this Policy and Guidelines, further more specific and stringent rules also apply to trading in Auckland Airport's securities, by Directors and certain employees

detail: Absolute ban, with no consent or waiver route, on any associated product limiting the economic risk of an unvested entitlement under an equity based remuneration scheme. It binds every person entitled to participate in such a scheme, not just Restricted Persons, and is not limited to listed products.
evidence: Where you are entitled to participate in any equity based remuneration scheme, you may not enter into any transaction for any associated product which has the effect of limiting the economic risk of participating in any unvested entitlement you are eligible for under that remuneration scheme.

detail: The associated products ban is drawn expressly around 'unvested entitlement', so once an entitlement has vested the ban falls away. There is no general hedging prohibition anywhere in the Policy.
evidence: which has the effect of limiting the economic risk of participating in any unvested entitlement you are eligible for under that remuneration scheme

section: Introduction and purpose; Trading outside black-out periods
detail: A hedge executed with listed instruments is a trade in Restricted Securities, so it needs written consent, valid 10 trading days, and must be outside a blackout period.
evidence: Before trading in Restricted Securities at any time outside of a blackout period, Restricted Persons must, in writing: notify Auckland Airport's General Manager Corporate Affairs of their intention to trade in securities, and seek consent to do so

section: Company Policy; Transaction in associated products
detail: An OTC collar over vested, unrestricted shares is neither an associated product over an unvested entitlement nor a trade in a listed security, so on the face of the Policy it is unregulated. That is a gap rather than an endorsement, and prudence points to seeking consent and disclosing the arrangement anyway, particularly given the 'If in doubt, don't' guidance and the NZ relevant-interest disclosure regime.
evidence: In this policy 'trade' includes buying or selling listed securities, or agreeing to do so, whether as principal or agent

section: Company Policy; Trading outside black-out periods
detail: Monetisation is not named. To the extent a prepaid forward or physically settled structure is an agreement to sell listed securities, it is a trade requiring written consent and cannot be entered during a blackout period; a purely cash-settled OTC structure sits outside the definition. If it monetises an unvested scheme entitlement it is prohibited outright as an associated product.
evidence: 'trade' includes buying or selling listed securities, or agreeing to do so

detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy and there is no speculative trading ban. A short sale of listed securities would still be a trade requiring consent for a Restricted Person, and closing it within a month would engage the short term trading rule.
Securities lending is not named and is outside the definition of 'trade', which covers only buying or selling listed securities or agreeing to do so.

CFDs are not named. A CFD over Auckland Airport shares is neither a listed security nor a listed derivative, so it is outside the definition of Restricted Securities and the consent regime, though the insider trading laws and the associated products rule would still bite where relevant.
evidence: any listed derivatives (including futures contracts listed on an authorised futures exchange) in respect of Auckland Airport securities

detail: There is no prohibition on, or consent requirement for, margin lending. The Policy positively contemplates it: the only reference is in the exclusions, which carve a lender's enforcement disposal out of the additional restrictions on Restricted Persons.
evidence: a disposal of Restricted Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

detail: The Policy contains no rule on granting a mortgage, charge, lien or other security over Auckland Airport securities, and creating an encumbrance is not 'buying or selling' and so not a trade requiring consent.

Secured financing over Auckland Airport shares is neither prohibited nor made subject to consent. The exclusions assume such arrangements exist and protect the executive from the consequences of a lender enforcing, which is the closest the Policy comes to addressing the topic.
evidence: The additional trading restriction for Restricted Persons (as contained in this Policy) does not apply to: ... a disposal of Restricted Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

detail: Expressed as 'you should not' rather than 'must not', with a one-month window, and relief requires three sign-offs: discussion with and approval by the General Manager Corporate Affairs, plus approval by General Counsel and one of the Chief Executive or Chief Financial Officer. The one-month period is unusually short compared with the market-standard three months.
evidence: You should not engage in short term trading (the buying or selling of listed securities within a one month period), unless there are exceptional circumstances discussed with and approved by Auckland Airport's General Manager Corporate Affairs and approved by General Counsel and one of the Chief Executive or the Chief Financial Officer.

detail: There is no separate derivatives rule, but 'VCX securities' is defined to include any derivatives entered into with a third party over or in relation to any VCX securities, which squarely captures an OTC put and call written by a bank. Dealing in them therefore requires the dual approvals in clause 4.2 and is barred during blackout periods.
evidence: VCX securities: Any Securities of Vicinity Centres and any derivatives entered into with a third party over or in relation to any VCX securities.

detail: Directors and employees who are not Restricted Officers need no approval, but because OTC derivatives are VCX securities they may not enter, close or vary them during a blackout period, and never while in possession of inside information.
evidence: Directors and employees may not deal, nor may they procure any other person to deal (including by giving hints or tips to that person), in VCX securities in any capacity

detail: Absolute ban, with no approval route, on hedging or any arrangement limiting exposure to risk relating to an element of remuneration that is unvested. Extends to Close Associates.
evidence: Restricted Officers and their Close Associates are prohibited from: ... hedging or entering into an arrangement that would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that is unvested, or which remains subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition

detail: The same absolute ban reaches remuneration that has vested but remains subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition, so a collar cannot be written over holding-locked or clawback-exposed plan securities.
evidence: an element of their remuneration that is unvested, or which remains subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition

detail: The hedging prohibition is tied to elements of remuneration that are unvested, restricted or forfeitable, so it does not reach shares that have vested free of restriction or were bought on market. Hedging those is not prohibited, but the derivative legs are VCX securities, so a Restricted Officer needs the clause 4.2 approvals and must act outside a blackout period.
evidence: Restricted Officers and their Close Associates may only deal in VCX securities after prior consultation with and approval by the appropriate persons

detail: Section 8 binds only Restricted Officers and their Close Associates; hedging by other directors and employees is not addressed, though any derivative is a VCX security subject to the blackout periods.

Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or collar-plus-loan over unrestricted vested securities is a dealing in VCX securities (as a third-party derivative) requiring the clause 4.2 approvals, and is not caught by the section 8 prohibitions unless it is properly described as a margin lending arrangement or takes a security interest over restricted vested securities. Over unvested or restricted remuneration it is prohibited outright.
evidence: any derivatives entered into with a third party over or in relation to any VCX securities

detail: Short selling is named as a form of prohibited speculative dealing, with no approval route, and extends to Close Associates.
evidence: engaging in speculative dealing in VCX securities, being short-selling VCX securities and short-term dealing

detail: The speculative dealing prohibition in section 8 is addressed only to Restricted Officers and their Close Associates.

Securities lending is not named anywhere in the Policy and there is no definition of dealing that would sweep it in, although lending stock to support a short position would engage the short-selling prohibition.

CFDs are not named. A CFD is a derivative entered into with a third party in relation to VCX securities and so a VCX security requiring clause 4.2 approvals, but a short CFD would breach the short-selling prohibition and one closed within 30 days would breach the short-term dealing prohibition, so approval is unlikely in practice.
evidence: any derivatives entered into with a third party over or in relation to any VCX securities

detail: Outright ban with no approval route on arrangements properly described as margin lending arrangements in relation to VCX securities, expressly including entering into one, transferring VCX securities into an existing margin loan account and selling VCX securities held in such an account. Because the sale limb is prohibited rather than merely gated, a margin call sale is a breach rather than a clearance question.
evidence: entering into arrangements properly described as margin lending arrangements in relation to VCX securities, which may include entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of VCX securities, transferring VCX securities into an existing margin loan account and selling VCX securities held in an existing margin loan account.

detail: The margin lending prohibition in section 8 binds only Restricted Officers and their Close Associates.
Any financial arrangement granting a security interest over vested VCX securities that remain subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition is banned outright, with no approval route.
evidence: entering into any financial arrangements whereby a security interest is granted in respect of any vested VCX Securities which remain subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition

detail: The security interest prohibition is deliberately confined to vested securities that remain subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition, so granting security over freely held vested securities is not prohibited. Granting a security interest is not itself characterised as dealing, so on the face of the Policy it does not even require clause 4.2 approval, though prudence and the reputational factor in clause 4.3.3 point to seeking it.
evidence: entering into any financial arrangements whereby a security interest is granted in respect of any vested VCX Securities which remain subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition

detail: Curiously the security interest prohibition names only vested securities, so granting security over unvested entitlements is not expressly addressed; in practice unvested plan entitlements are not capable of being charged and any arrangement limiting risk on them is banned by the hedging limb.

The Policy has no general secured financing prohibition. A bespoke bank facility secured on unrestricted vested VCX securities is caught only if it is 'properly described as a margin lending arrangement', which a bilateral term loan with a fixed advance and no maintenance margin ordinarily is not. The absence of any forced-sale exclusion means lender enforcement during a blackout would nonetheless be a dealing in breach of section 3.
evidence: entering into arrangements properly described as margin lending arrangements in relation to VCX securities

detail: Financing secured on vested securities that remain subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition is banned outright by the security interest limb, whatever the form of the facility.
evidence: entering into any financial arrangements whereby a security interest is granted in respect of any vested VCX Securities which remain subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition

detail: Section 8 binds only Restricted Officers and their Close Associates; secured financing by other directors and employees is not addressed.

A 30-day round-trip test, applying in both directions (buy then sell, or sell then buy) and across any VCX securities rather than the same parcel. Because VCX securities include third-party derivatives, opening and closing a derivative position within 30 days, or dealing in shares within 30 days of an option leg, is caught. There is no carve-out for shares acquired on vesting.
evidence: short-term dealing (i.e. if a person buys (or sells) VCX securities on a date and then sells (or buys) any VCX securities on a date that is less than 30 days after the first dealing)

detail: The short-term dealing prohibition applies only to Restricted Officers and their Close Associates.

Absolute ban, with no venue limit and no approval route, on any use of Derivatives over unvested Equity Interests by Company Personnel holding them and by their Connected Persons. Derivatives is defined to include put and call options and 'caps and collars', so a collar over unvested shares, options or performance rights is squarely caught.
evidence: Company Personnel with Equity Interests and their Connected Persons are not permitted to use Derivatives in relation to any unvested Company's Securities in any way.

detail: Company Personnel who are not Designated Personnel may use Derivatives, including OTC puts, calls and collars, over vested Company Securities subject only to the General Prohibition, the 'front page' test and the balance of the policy. No notice or approval is required of them.
evidence: Company Personnel and their Connected Persons may use Derivatives in relation to vested Company's Securities, provided any Trading complies with the balance of this policy.

detail: Derivatives over vested Securities are expressly allowed, but for Designated Personnel entry into the derivative is Trading that must occur inside an Approved Trading Period and requires prior approval from the Managing Director and Company Secretary, plus written confirmation to the Company Secretary within 2 business days of completion.
evidence: Other Designated Personnel of the Company must seek approval from the Managing Director and Company Secretary prior to them or their Connected Persons undertaking the Trade.

detail: A director may enter a Derivative over vested Securities in an Approved Trading Period after informing the Chair (the Chair informs the Chair of the Audit, Risk & Compliance Committee); no approval is required, only prior notice, followed by written advice to the Company Secretary within 2 business days for ASX notification within 5 business days.
evidence: A director of the Company must inform the Chair prior to them or their Connected Persons undertaking the Trade;

detail: The rationale given is that hedging unvested equity would allow value to be realised even if performance hurdles are not met and would break the connection between staff performance and shareholder interests. 'Any other hedging or investment arrangement' falls within the defined term Derivatives, so the ban is not limited to listed instruments.
evidence: The use of Derivatives over unvested Company's Securities may allow value to be realised from those Securities even if performance hurdles have not been met. This would break the intended connection between staff performance and shareholder best interests.

detail: Hedging of vested Securities is expressly permitted rather than merely unaddressed, because 'any other hedging or investment arrangement' is a Derivative and section 7 permits Derivatives over vested Securities. Subject to Approved Trading Periods, prior approval or notice, the speculative trading ban and the 'front page' test.
evidence: Company Personnel and their Connected Persons may use Derivatives in relation to vested Company's Securities, provided any Trading complies with the balance of this policy.

detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward, structured financial product or collar is within the definition of Derivatives and its entry is Trading (an agreement to sell or grant an option), so it is permitted over vested Securities but only in an Approved Trading Period with prior approval. Note that a short-dated forward risks being caught by the speculative trading ban, which names forward contracts as short term Trading.
evidence: Trading means taking part in any transaction associated with applying for, buying, acquiring, selling, disposing, granting an option, converting, assigning rights to buy, sell or subscribe for, or agreeing to do any of these things

detail: Any monetisation of unvested Equity Interests would be effected through a Derivative (forward, structured financial product, collar or 'any other hedging or investment arrangement') and is therefore banned outright.
evidence: Company Personnel with Equity Interests and their Connected Persons are not permitted to use Derivatives in relation to any unvested Company's Securities in any way.

detail: Outright ban on Designated Personnel and their Connected Persons. The policy defines short selling narrowly as borrowing a security and selling it in the hope of buying it back lower, so a covered collar over shares actually held is not short selling on the policy's own definition.
evidence: Designated Personnel and their Connected Persons must not engage in short selling of the Company's securities.

detail: Section 10 is directed only at Designated Personnel; Company Personnel who are not Designated Personnel are not covered by an express short selling ban.
Securities lending is not named anywhere and is not within the definition of Trading. Borrowing securities is mentioned only descriptively in explaining what short selling is.

Contracts for difference and spread bets are expressly named as Derivatives. They are permitted in principle over vested Securities under section 7, but in practice a CFD over Company Securities is short term Trading caught by the speculative trading ban and, if short, by the short selling ban.
evidence: Designated Personnel and their Connected Persons must not engage in speculative Trading in the Company's securities, such as Trading on considerations of a short term nature.

detail: Flat ban on Designated Personnel and their Connected Persons entering margin loans or any margin lending arrangements in respect of Company Securities, with no vesting-state qualification, no approval route and no exemption. evidence: Designated Personnel or their Connected Person are prohibited from entering into margin loans or any margin lending arrangements in respect of Company's Securities.

detail: Section 8 binds only Designated Personnel and their Connected Persons; the policy says nothing about margin lending by other Company Personnel.

Granting a mortgage, charge, lien or pledge over Company Securities is not mentioned, and the definition of Trading covers buying, selling, disposing, granting an option, converting and assigning rights but not the creation of a security interest. Speculative Trading is banned, defined to include buying and selling Securities within a six month period and entering into other short term Trading, with forward contracts given as the example. Sale of shares received on vesting of employee incentives is carved out. This makes instrument tenor material: a collar maturing inside six months, or one written as a short-dated forward, is exposed to this prohibition.
evidence: This includes buying and selling Securities within a six month period, and entering into other short term Trading (e.g. forward contracts).

detail: Section 9 applies only to Designated Personnel and their Connected Persons.

evidence: Team Members participating in any of The Lottery Corporation's employee or executive equity or incentive plans and each of their Associates, are prohibited from: ... entering into a derivative arrangement in respect of restricted shares and unvested performance options or rights granted under these plans.

evidence: any derivatives of those Securities, including equity swaps, contracts for difference, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options, whether settled by cash or otherwise

detail: Same position as Directors, with pre-clearance from the Company Secretary or MD & CEO (ELT members: the Company Secretary, or the MD & CEO and the Chairman). Pre-clearance may be refused without reasons and may be refused for non-compliance with the applicable Minimum Shareholding Policy.
evidence: A Director or Restricted Employee who wishes to Trade in The Lottery Corporation Securities at any time must obtain written pre-clearance

evidence: prohibited from: hedging the value of restricted shares and unvested performance options or rights;

detail: The hedging prohibition is confined by its terms to restricted shares and unvested awards, so hedging vested unrestricted shares is not prohibited. evidence: Caltex staff who are not Designated Caltex Personnel may trade in Caltex securities at any time provided they do not have or possess any inside information.

section: Trading Restrictions - Hedging Transactions; Margin Lending and other secured financing arrangements
detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and collar-plus-loan structures are not named. Each has the effect of limiting risk exposure to Caltex securities and so falls within the hedging ban, and if the advance is secured on the shares it is separately caught by the secured financing prohibition.
evidence: prohibited from entering into any arrangements that would have the effect of limiting their risk exposure relating to Caltex securities

detail: Flat ban on entering into any arrangements for short selling Caltex securities, with no approval route or security-state carve-out. The reference to 'any arrangements' would reach synthetic short exposure as well as physical short sales.
evidence: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from entering into any arrangements for short selling Caltex securities.

detail: Securities lending is not named. A stock loan transfers the legal interest in the security and is therefore a 'trade', so it would need clearance, fall outside closed periods and be notified within three days; it is not separately prohibited unless it forms part of a short selling or risk-limiting arrangement.
evidence: "trade" includes subscribing for, buying, selling or otherwise transferring the beneficial or legal interest in a security.

section: Trading Restrictions - Trading in Derivatives, Short-term Trading, Short Selling, Hedging Transactions
detail: Contracts for differences are expressly brought within the policy, so they are trades requiring clearance rather than being outside it. In practice most CFD positions are separately prohibited: a short CFD by the short selling ban, a risk-limiting CFD by the hedging ban, and any CFD closed out within six months by the short-term trading ban.
evidence: This policy applies to transactions in derivative markets and trading involving derivative products (including warrants, exchange traded options, over-the-counter options and contracts for differences)

section: Trading Restrictions - Margin Lending and other secured financing arrangements
detail: Margin lending in respect of Caltex securities is expressly prohibited at all times for all Designated Caltex Personnel, with no approval route, no vesting carve-out and no grandfathering.
evidence: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from entering into any margin lending and other secured financing arrangements in respect of Caltex securities.

section: Trading Restrictions - Margin Lending and other secured financing arrangements
detail: Granting security over Caltex securities to support financing is prohibited as a secured financing arrangement. A charge, lien or pledge unconnected with any financing is not named, and the definition of 'trade' does not expressly sweep in the creation of a security interest.
evidence: prohibited from entering into any margin lending and other secured financing arrangements in respect of Caltex securities.

section: Trading Restrictions - Margin Lending and other secured financing arrangements
detail: The prohibition is deliberately wider than margin loans, extending to 'other secured financing arrangements in respect of Caltex securities'. It binds every Director and CLT member regardless of security state, has no clearance or waiver route, and the exceptional circumstances discretion is confined to closed period trading.
evidence: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from entering into any margin lending and other secured financing arrangements in respect of Caltex securities.

detail: Six month ban on short-term or speculative trading, expressly extended to derivative products issued over or in respect of Caltex securities, with purchase and sale of the same securities within six months given as an inclusive example. No stated matching basis and no carve-out for plan securities.
evidence: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from engaging in short term or speculative trading in Caltex securities or derivative products issued over or in respect of Caltex securities, including purchasing and selling the same Caltex securities within a six month period.

detail: The policy expressly contemplates derivatives over Reece shares by permitting Directors to hedge their shareholdings, with equity swaps and contracts for differences named as examples of hedging instruments. Entry, renewal, alteration and close-out each require compliance with clause 6.1: advance written notice, written clearance acknowledgement from the Chair or Company Secretary, outside a black-out period, and no price sensitive information. There is no venue restriction, so an over-the-counter put and call with a bank are within the permission.
evidence: Directors and Executives are only permitted to hedge their shareholdings: In compliance with section 6.1 above; and Providing the hedge transaction is not entered into, renewed, altered or closed out when the Director or Executive is in possession of price sensitive information.

detail: Same position as Directors for shares that have been acquired on exercise and are free of any transfer restriction, except clearance comes from the MD and Group CEO or Company Secretary.
evidence: Executives must give advance notice and receive clearance acknowledgement (e.g. by way of exchange of emails) from the MD and Group CEO or Company Secretary before commencing to deal in Company Securities

detail: Employees who are not Directors or Executives are outside the section 6 clearance and hedging provisions. They may deal outside black-out periods without inside information and without clearance; the three month short-term dealing ban in 5.3 still binds them, and forward contracts are named there as prohibited short-term dealings.
evidence: At any time other than during a black-out period, Employees (other than Directors and Executives) may deal in securities in the Company but only if you do not have inside information.

detail: Hedging of a Director's shareholding is expressly permitted, subject only to clause 6.1 clearance and to the requirement that entry, renewal, alteration and close-out do not occur while holding price sensitive information. The bar on hedging Plan equity awards is directed at Executives; a Director who receives Plan equity would also meet the 'Executives' definition and be caught by it. There is no absolute hedging prohibition anywhere in the policy.
evidence: Directors and Executives are only permitted to hedge their shareholdings: In compliance with section 6.1 above; and Providing the hedge transaction is not entered into, renewed, altered or closed out when the Director or Executive is in possession of price sensitive information.

detail: Absolute bar on hedging equity awards granted under a Plan before the rights are exercised. No clearance route and no exceptional circumstances relief.
evidence: However, Executives are not permitted to hedge equity awards granted under a Plan prior to exercising those rights or, once exercised, while the securities are subject to a transfer restriction.

detail: The bar continues after exercise for as long as the resulting securities are subject to a transfer restriction, so shares still inside a holding lock cannot be collared.
evidence: or, once exercised, while the securities are subject to a transfer restriction.

detail: Once Plan awards have been exercised and the resulting securities are free of any transfer restriction, the specific bar falls away and the general permission applies: hedging is allowed with clearance from the MD and Group CEO or Company Secretary, outside black-out periods and with no price sensitive information at entry, renewal, alteration or close-out.
evidence: Directors and Executives are only permitted to hedge their shareholdings: In compliance with section 6.1 above

detail: Section 6.2 regulates hedging only by Directors and Executives. The policy says nothing about hedging by other Employees, who are otherwise free to deal outside black-out periods without inside information.

Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward, collar or similar is a transaction, arrangement or financial product operating to limit the economic risk of a Reece shareholding and so is hedging, permitted with clause 6.1 clearance. The counterweight is clause 5.3, which gives forward contracts as an example of prohibited short-term dealings, so a short-dated monetisation is at risk of being characterised as prohibited short-term dealing.
evidence: hedging includes the entry into any transaction, arrangement or financial product which operates to limit the economic risk of a security holding in the Company

detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the policy and there is no prohibited dealings list. Only the three month short-term dealing ban and the insider trading prohibition would apply.
Securities lending is not named and is not caught by the section 4.1 description of trading or dealing, which is confined to buying, selling, subscribing and agreements to do so.

Contracts for differences are expressly named as an example of a hedging instrument, so a CFD over a Director's or Executive's shareholding is permitted with clause 6.1 clearance. A CFD closed out within three months would engage the short-term dealing ban, and an Executive may not use one over unvested or transfer-restricted Plan securities.
evidence: includes financial instruments such as equity swaps and contracts for differences.

detail: Margin lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy, for any tier or security state, and there is no requirement to notify or obtain approval for it.

Granting security, a charge, mortgage, lien or pledge over Company securities is not mentioned, and the section 4.1 description of trading or dealing (buy, sell, subscribe, or agree to do so) does not sweep it in.
The policy contains no secured financing provision of any kind: no ban, no clearance requirement, no disclosure obligation and no guidance on forced sales by a lender during a black-out period.

Directors and Employees must not round-trip Company securities within three months in either direction, and must not enter into any other short-term dealings, with forward contracts given as an express example. No stated matching basis and no carve-out for Plan securities or for the exercise of equity awards.
evidence: Directors and Employees must not buy and sell or sell and buy securities in the Company within a three-month period or enter into any other short-term dealings in Company securities (for example, forward contracts).

detail: The definition of Company securities is confined to Company-issued instruments (shares, debentures, units of shares and rights or options to acquire or subscribe for shares), and 'deal' is confined to subscribing, purchasing, selling and agreements to do so, so a bank-written option is not itself a Company security. Paragraph 15 nonetheless regulates derivatives economically by requiring prior consent for any transaction or arrangement which operates to limit the economic risk of a holding, with no venue limit, so an over-the-counter put and call over vested unrestricted shares require the prior consent of the Managing Director (or the Chairman of the Board for the Managing Director) and post-trade confirmation.
evidence: A Restricted Person or Connected Person may not deal in Company securities or enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their holdings of Company securities (known as Hedging) without the prior consent of the Managing Director or Chairman of the Board in the case of the Managing Director before commencing the transaction.

detail: Employees who are not Restricted Persons need only notify the Company Secretary before and after a transaction; the paragraph 15 consent requirement binds Restricted Persons and Connected Persons only, and the Board would have to make a specific determination to prohibit Hedging by anyone else.
evidence: Employees other than Restricted Persons may deal in Company securities at any time if the employee notifies the Company Secretary before commencing the transaction and after the transaction has occurred, providing confirmation of the trading.

detail: Hedging is not banned outright for ordinary shareholdings: it requires the prior consent of the Managing Director (or the Chairman of the Board where the Managing Director is hedging), and subsequent confirmation of the trading, including trading by a Connected Person. The policy records that Hedging is 'generally speaking discouraged', so consent is discretionary and may be refused or made conditional without reasons.
evidence: Generally speaking Hedging is discouraged and is explicitly prohibited in relation to participation in any securities-based remuneration plan or scheme operated by the Company.

detail: Hedging is explicitly prohibited in relation to participation in any securities-based remuneration plan or scheme operated by the Company, which covers unvested options and rights held under those plans. The only route around it would be the paragraph 14 exceptional circumstances discretion.
evidence: Hedging ... is explicitly prohibited in relation to participation in any securities-based remuneration plan or scheme operated by the Company.

detail: The same explicit prohibition applies while securities remain part of participation in a securities-based remuneration plan or scheme. Shares received on exercise may not be sold other than in accordance with the policy's procedures, so shares still held under plan arrangements should be treated as outside the collar.
evidence: explicitly prohibited in relation to participation in any securities-based remuneration plan or scheme operated by the Company.

detail: Paragraph 15 binds Restricted Persons and Connected Persons. Employees outside those tiers may hedge subject only to the paragraph 18 notification duty and the insider trading prohibition, unless and until the Board exercises its discretion to prohibit them.
evidence: The Board may, in its discretion, determine that other persons are prohibited from Hedging.

detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and collar-plus-loan structures are not named. Each is an arrangement operating to limit the economic risk of a holding and so falls within Hedging, requiring prior consent and post-trade confirmation. A structure that in substance sells the shares within 12 months would also engage the short-term trading ban.
evidence: enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their holdings of Company securities (known as Hedging) without the prior consent of the Managing Director

detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the policy. A short position would in practice be caught by the 12 month short-term trading ban for Restricted Persons and by the Front Page Test general principle.
Securities lending is not named, and the definition of 'deal' is confined to subscribing for, purchasing or selling Company securities or agreeing to do those things.

CFDs are not named. A CFD written against an existing holding is an arrangement limiting economic risk and so is Hedging requiring prior consent; a speculative CFD closed out within 12 months would breach the short-term trading ban and would be difficult to reconcile with the Front Page Test.
evidence: transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their holdings of Company securities (known as Hedging)

detail: There is no margin lending clause. The nearest provision is the general principle that personal trading must not use broker credit and must settle on relevant exchange settlement terms and industry standards, which bars buying Company securities on credit extended by a broker. It is directed at settlement of trades rather than at a third party lender taking security over an existing holding, and the accompanying principle that trading be on a scale reflecting the individual's ability to fund and maintain the portfolio points the same way.
evidence: do not utilise broker credit - relevant exchange settlement terms must apply on all occasions and all transactions must be settled according to industry standards;

detail: Granting security, a charge, mortgage, lien or pledge over Company securities is not mentioned, is not within the definition of 'deal', and triggers no notification or consent obligation.

The policy contains no secured financing provision: no prohibition, no consent requirement, no disclosure obligation and no treatment of a lender's forced sale during a Blackout Period. Only the broker credit principle in paragraph 11(f) and the perception-based Front Page Test bear on the question.

An unusually long 12 month intention test binding Restricted Persons and Connected Persons at all times, catching both a purchase with a view to resale and a sale with a view to repurchase within 12 months. The only carve-out is the sale of shares acquired on conversion of a security where the combined holding periods of the security and the resulting shares exceed 12 months. Paragraph 14 allows the Managing Director or Chairman to approve dealings that would otherwise be prohibited, so this ban is in principle waivable.
evidence: Restricted Persons and Connected Persons may never engage in short term trading of any Company securities. In general, the purchase of securities with a view to resale within a 12 month period and the sale of securities with a view to repurchase within a 12 month period would be considered to be transactions of a "short term" nature.

detail: Absolute ban for every Employee and Connected Person on transactions in exchange-traded or other organised-market puts, calls or derivative securities over Company securities. No vesting distinction, no approval route and no exemption; section 5 excluded dealings disapply only sections 4.1 and 4.3.
evidence: Employees may not engage in transactions in publicly traded options in the Company's securities, such as puts, calls or derivative securities, on an exchange or in any other organised market.

detail: A bilateral OTC put or call with a bank is not a 'publicly traded option' and so falls outside 3.4, but any OTC derivative that limits the economic risk of holding Company securities, or is designed to offset a decrease in their market price, is prohibited hedging under 3.5. The definition of securities expressly includes put and call options whether or not issued by the Company, so an OTC option is itself a Company security and dealing in it by a Restricted Person would also require approval and fall in blackouts were it not already banned.
evidence: You may not enter into hedging or monetisation transactions or similar arrangements designed to hedge or offset any decrease in the market price of the Company's securities.

detail: Blanket ban on arrangements that limit the economic risk of holding Company securities. The policy draws no distinction between unvested, vested-but-locked and freely held securities, applies to Connected Persons, and provides no clearance or hardship route out of section 3.
evidence: Hedging includes entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding the Company's securities. You may not enter into hedging or monetisation transactions or similar arrangements designed to hedge or offset any decrease in the market price of the Company's securities.

detail: Monetisation transactions are named alongside hedging and banned outright, so a prepaid forward, collar-plus-loan or similar cash-out structure is prohibited for all Employees irrespective of vesting or tier.
evidence: You may not enter into hedging or monetisation transactions or similar arrangements designed to hedge or offset any decrease in the market price of the Company's securities.

detail: Speculative dealing is banned and short selling is named as an instance of it; the policy defines short selling as borrowing and selling securities to buy them back lower.
evidence: Employees must not deal in the Company's securities on a speculative basis, including short-selling.

detail: Directors and Section 16 Officers are additionally responsible for the statutory US restrictions on short sales of the Company's securities under Section 16 of the Exchange Act.
evidence: Directors and Section 16 Officers are also responsible for compliance with Section 16 of the Exchange Act (including provisions related to disgorgement of "short-swing profits" and restrictions on short sales of the Company's securities)

detail: Lending out Company securities is never mentioned; borrowing securities appears only in the descriptive definition of short selling. The dealing definition (purchases, sales, gifts, donations, acquisitions, disposals and option exercises) does not sweep in a securities loan, although a lending arrangement that transferred title would be a disposal.

CFDs are not named. A CFD over Company securities is speculative dealing, is a derivative security if written on an organised market, and if short is both a hedge of a decrease in price and economically a short sale, so it is caught by three separate bans.
evidence: Employees must not deal in the Company's securities on a speculative basis, including short-selling.

detail: Holding Company securities in a margin account is prohibited for all Employees and Connected Persons. The only carve-out is the cashless exercise of options, where shares underlying the option are sold to fund tax, the exercise price and broker commissions.
evidence: You may not hold the Company's securities in a margin account or pledge the Company's securities as collateral for a loan.

detail: Pledging Company securities as collateral for a loan is expressly banned. A charge, lien or security interest unconnected with a loan is not named, and granting security is not part of the dealing definition, so it is only caught if it amounts to a pledge for a loan.
evidence: You may not hold the Company's securities in a margin account or pledge the Company's securities as collateral for a loan.

detail: Any loan collateralised by Company securities is prohibited, not merely a margin loan. The ban sits in section 3 (all Employees), has no tier or vesting carve-out, and is not among the section 5 excluded dealings, which relieve only the blackout and approval requirements in sections 4.1 and 4.3.
evidence: You may not hold the Company's securities in a margin account or pledge the Company's securities as collateral for a loan.

detail: No holding period or minimum interval is set. The restraint is qualitative: dealing on a speculative basis is banned, reinforced by the Front Page Test, and approval will not be granted where a dealing would fail that test.
evidence: Employees must not deal in the Company's securities on a speculative basis, including short-selling.

detail: Directors and Section 16 Officers must comply with the US short-swing profit rule, under which profits on a purchase and sale (in either order) matched within six months are disgorgeable. This is imported by reference rather than being stated as a policy holding period.
evidence: Directors and Section 16 Officers are also responsible for compliance with Section 16 of the Exchange Act (including provisions related to disgorgement of "short-swing profits" ...) and Rule 144 of the Securities Act of 1933 in connection with their transactions in the Company's securities.

detail: Restricted Persons inherit every section 3 prohibition and add blackout periods and prior approval. Even if a derivative escaped sections 3.4 and 3.5, it would be a dealing in securities (the definition of securities includes put and call options whether or not issued by the Company) requiring Chief Legal Officer approval and barred in the quarterly and event-specific blackouts.
evidence: During any period that is not a trading blackout period under section 4.1, Restricted Persons must, prior to any proposed dealing, seek approval for the proposed dealing in the Company's securities.

detail: Company Securities expressly include over-the-counter options, equity swaps, futures and hedges, whether cash settled or not, and Dealing expressly includes granting, accepting, acquiring, disposing, exercising or discharging an option or other right or obligation. Buying a put from a bank and writing a call to it are therefore each a Dealing in Company Securities: permitted outside Prohibited Periods with prior written clearance from the relevant Approving Officer. If the derivative is protective it must additionally clear Section 7.3.
evidence: Company Securities means all securities issued by the Company, and includes shares, share rights, performance rights, options, and derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise.

detail: Exchange-traded options, share warrants and similar instruments are named as prohibited where they are short term or speculative. A long-dated, non-speculative exchange-traded derivative is not caught by 7.2 and would fall back to being a Dealing requiring clearance, but the qualifier is applied by the Approving Officer together with the front page test.
evidence: This prohibition includes short term direct dealing in Company Securities, including derivative market transactions involving exchange-trade options, share warrants, contracts for difference, and other similar instruments, which are short term or speculative.

detail: Any derivative that operates as a protection arrangement over unvested Company Securities, or securities subject to a holding lock, is banned outright with no clearance route. Derivatives that are not protective remain Dealings requiring clearance.
evidence: The entering into of all types of "protection arrangements" for any Company Securities: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

detail: Absolute ban, at any time, on protection arrangements over unvested Company Securities; the definition reaches securities held beneficially on the Restricted Person's behalf, for example in trust or under an incentive plan. No Approving Officer discretion is available.
evidence: The entering into of all types of "protection arrangements" for any Company Securities: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

detail: Securities that have vested but remain subject to a holding lock or holding term (for example performance-based remuneration not yet released) are treated identically to unvested securities: protection arrangements over them are prohibited at any time. Release from the holding lock is itself an excluded dealing, after which the vested_unrestricted rule applies.
evidence: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

detail: For securities that are neither unvested nor subject to a holding lock, a protection arrangement is expressly permitted subject to approval under Section 6: prior written request to the relevant Approving Officer copied to the Company Secretary, written clearance valid five business days and withdrawable, outside Blackout Periods and any Additional Period, and satisfying the front page test.
evidence: The entering into of all types of "protection arrangements" for any Company Securities: ... and otherwise, requires approval under Section 6.

detail: Monetisation is not named. A collar, prepaid forward or similar cash-out over vested unrestricted securities is a protection arrangement (it limits the economic risk of the holding) requiring approval under Section 6, and if it is secured on the securities the loan leg separately requires clearance under 7.4. Over unvested or holding-lock securities the same structure is prohibited outright.
evidence: operate to limit the economic risk of any Restricted Person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including Company Securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under an incentive plan) on that Restricted Person's behalf

detail: Short selling is listed as a species of protection arrangement, so it is banned outright in respect of unvested or holding-lock securities.
evidence: "protection arrangements" include transactions which: amount to "short selling" of Company Securities

detail: Unusually, the policy does not ban short selling outright. Because it is drafted as a protection arrangement, short selling of securities that are not unvested or holding-locked 'otherwise requires approval under Section 6'. In practice a short sale would be speculative trading contrary to 7.2 and would fail the front page test, so clearance should not be expected.
evidence: otherwise, requires approval under Section 6.

detail: Securities lending or borrowing is nowhere mentioned and is not within the Deal definition (applying for, acquiring or disposing; agreements to do so; granting or exercising options and rights). A stock loan that transferred title would be a disposal and so a Dealing, but the policy does not say so.

Contracts for difference are named in the speculative trading ban. The prohibition is qualified by the words 'which are short term or speculative', and a short CFD would independently be a protection arrangement enabling profit from a price decrease, prohibited over unvested or holding-lock securities and otherwise requiring Section 6 approval.
evidence: This prohibition includes short term direct dealing in Company Securities, including derivative market transactions involving exchange-trade options, share warrants, contracts for difference, and other similar instruments, which are short term or speculative.

detail: Margin loans are not banned; they require prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer under the Section 6 procedure. No vesting distinction is drawn in 7.4 itself, and a disposal resulting from the secured lender exercising its rights is an excluded dealing under 5.1.
evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer in accordance with the procedure set out in Section 6.

detail: Granting security is not itself within the Deal definition, but taking Company Securities as collateral for any secured lending arrangement is expressly routed through Section 6 clearance. A charge or lien unconnected with lending is not addressed.
evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer

detail: The clause is not confined to margin loans: 'or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities' captures a bank loan secured on collared shares. It is a clearance requirement, not a prohibition, and the Approving Officer may seek input from KMP and Senior Employees on reputational and governance implications before deciding.
evidence: margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities

detail: Qualitative ban with no stated holding period or matching window: short-term or speculative trading is prohibited 'under no circumstances', expressly extending to derivative market transactions that are short term or speculative.
evidence: Under no circumstances should Restricted Persons engage in short-term or speculative trading in the Company's Securities.

detail: For employees who are not Designated Officers the only constraint on derivatives is the insider trading prohibition, which is expressly extended to third-party products created over Sonic securities and to options limiting economic risk. There is no window, clearance or hedging restriction on this tier.
evidence: The prohibitions described above also apply to trading in financial products issued or created over Sonic's securities by third parties, and to trading in associated products and products such as options which operate to limit the economic risk of security holdings in Sonic.

detail: An OTC put or call written over Sonic securities is a financial product created over Sonic's securities by a third party, so trading in it is caught by 2.1 and by the 2.2 window restriction. No pre-clearance is required inside a window (except for sales by the Managing Director and Finance Director), but details must be given to the Company Secretary within 24 hours of execution.
evidence: Designated Officers are only permitted to trade in the period of eight weeks commencing on the business day after the public announcement of half year and year end results, and the period of five weeks commencing on the business day after Sonic's Annual General Meeting.

detail: Exchange-traded options and derivatives are within the definition of Sonic securities ('shares, options, derivatives, debt securities and any other financial products that are able to be traded on a financial market') and so may only be traded in an open window, free of inside information, and must be notified within 24 hours. Short-dated or short positions remain barred by the short-term trading and short selling prohibition.
evidence: Sonic Employees are prohibited from buying or selling or otherwise trading Sonic securities (including shares, options, derivatives, debt securities and any other financial products that are able to be traded on a financial market) at any time

detail: A derivative that limits the economic risk of participating in unvested equity scheme entitlements is banned outright, with no window or approval route. Derivatives that are not risk-limiting are not caught by this clause but remain subject to the window restriction.
evidence: Designated Officers are also prohibited from entering into: transactions in products which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements or entitlements subject to a holding lock under any equity based remuneration schemes

detail: Absolute prohibition on hedging unvested equity based remuneration entitlements; no exception, approval or hardship route is provided, and breach triggers forfeiture of equity rewards.
evidence: transactions in products which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements or entitlements subject to a holding lock under any equity based remuneration schemes

detail: Entitlements subject to a holding lock are treated the same as unvested entitlements, so shares delivered under an equity scheme but still locked cannot be hedged or collared until the lock is released.
evidence: entitlements subject to a holding lock under any equity based remuneration schemes

detail: The hedging ban is confined to unvested and holding-locked equity scheme entitlements. Hedging shares that are fully vested and free of a holding lock, or shares bought on market, is not prohibited; it is simply trading in a product that limits economic risk, permitted only within an open window, only if free of inside information, and notifiable to the Company Secretary within 24 hours.
evidence: trading in associated products and products such as options which operate to limit the economic risk of security holdings in Sonic

detail: The prohibition on hedging unvested or holding-locked entitlements is expressed to bind Designated Officers only. Employees below that threshold are restrained only by the insider trading prohibition as extended to risk-limiting products.
evidence: Designated Officers are also prohibited from entering into: transactions in products which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements

detail: Monetisation is not named. A collar, prepaid forward or similar over vested unlocked shares is trading in a product that limits economic risk of a Sonic holding, permitted only inside an open window and notifiable within 24 hours. If secured on the shares, the Director secured financing approval in 2.2 also applies. Over unvested or holding-locked entitlements the same structure is prohibited.
evidence: products such as options which operate to limit the economic risk of security holdings in Sonic

detail: Outright ban on short selling arrangements in Sonic securities for Designated Officers and their connected persons, with no approval route.
evidence: Designated Officers are also prohibited from entering into: ... short-term trading and short selling arrangements in Sonic securities.

detail: The short selling prohibition is drafted as a Designated Officer prohibition in 2.2; the General Prohibitions in 2.1 do not mention short selling, so it is not addressed for employees generally.
Securities lending or borrowing is not mentioned anywhere in the policy, for any tier, and the trading concept is not defined in a way that expressly captures it.

CFDs are not named. A CFD is a financial product created over Sonic's securities by a third party and so within 2.1; a short CFD is a short selling arrangement and is typically short-term trading, both prohibited for Designated Officers. A long CFD would fall back to the window restriction.
evidence: short-term trading and short selling arrangements in Sonic securities.

detail: Margin lending is not banned for directors: it requires prior approval of the Chair (or, for the Chair, the Chair of the Remuneration and Nomination Committee) and disclosure of the arrangement to the Board. The policy is silent on margin calls, forced sales and price triggers.
evidence: Directors of Sonic Healthcare Limited are also prohibited from entering into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in relation to Sonic securities without the prior approval of the Chair (and for the Chair, the Chair of the Remuneration and Nomination Committee) and disclosure of such arrangements to the Board.

detail: The margin lending and secured financing clause is expressly confined to 'Directors of Sonic Healthcare Limited'. For Designated Officers who are not directors, including subsidiary CEOs and senior finance and corporate staff, the policy imposes no margin lending restriction at all.

Granting security over Sonic securities is not itself described as trading, but a director who charges or pledges shares to support a financing is entering a secured financing arrangement in relation to Sonic securities and so needs Chair approval and must disclose it to the Board. A charge unconnected with financing is not addressed.
evidence: margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in relation to Sonic securities without the prior approval of the Chair

detail: The wording extends beyond margin loans to 'other secured financing arrangements in relation to Sonic securities', which captures a bank loan secured on collared shares. Two conditions: prior approval of the Chair (Chair of the Remuneration and Nomination Committee for the Chair) and disclosure of the arrangement to the Board. No timing, quantum, loan-to-value or price-trigger conditions are stated.
evidence: Directors of Sonic Healthcare Limited are also prohibited from entering into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in relation to Sonic securities without the prior approval of the Chair ... and disclosure of such arrangements to the Board.

detail: No secured financing restriction applies to non-director Designated Officers or to Sonic Employees generally; the clause binds directors only.

Short-term trading arrangements in Sonic securities are prohibited outright for Designated Officers. No holding period, matching rule or definition of 'short-term' is given, so the characterisation is left to the approver's judgment.

detail: Derivatives are never named. A bank-written OTC put or call over existing stapled securities therefore falls outside both definitions unless it hedges restricted remuneration or is part of a secured financing, and physical settlement would be a Dealing requiring a Trading Window and notification.
